name: pdk-isodate-etl
instr:
Our maintenance planner now gets its windows from the vendor's calendar export as ISO 8601 time intervals, and isodate has nothing that reads them. Please add `isodate.parse_interval(text)`, returning a `(start, end)` tuple.

A window is written as start/end, start/duration or duration/end. Every date or date and time written out in full has to come back exactly as `parse_date` or `parse_datetime` returns it, so dates stay dates and offsets are kept. A duration is read the way `parse_duration` reads it, and the missing bound is the other one moved by it with isodate's `Duration` arithmetic (2026-01-31 plus P1M is 2026-02-28).

A sample of Monday's export is in /data/windows/. Its duration_min column is the length the vendor computed for each window, in minutes. Every row has to parse to a start and end that far apart, and so does any other window the vendor writes the same way.

Text that doesn't give a valid window, including a window that ends before it starts, has to raise `isodate.ISO8601Error` and never another exception. isodate's existing functions and the tests in /app/tests have to keep working as they do now. There's no network here.
